findings.summary: Controlled vs uncontrolled components (Q8) depend on refs, which are not taught until Q23-Q24 on page 6.
findings.fix: Add a one-line gloss on page 3 ("a ref is a handle to the DOM node, covered on page 6"), or move Q8 after Context and Refs.

findings.summary: Props vs state (Q5-Q7) use useState, state and setters before the State and useState page (page 4) teaches them.
findings.evidence: Q7 example: "const [n, setN] = useState(0);" and Q5 "const [n] = useState(0);" appear before Q9 "How does useState work"
findings.fix: Add a short note on page 3 that useState returns [value, setter] and is covered in detail on page 4, or reorder State before Components and Props.

findings.summary: Q22 tells the learner to fix Context re-renders with useMemo, which is not defined until Q25 on page 7.
findings.evidence: "**Memoize** the value with `useMemo`" and example `const value = useMemo(() => ({ user, theme }), [user, theme]);`
findings.fix: Add a one-line explanation of useMemo ("caches a value between renders; see page 7") at Q22, or move the memoization page before Context.

findings.summary: Q29 (custom hook rules) depends on the Rules of Hooks, which are only defined in the next question, Q30.
findings.evidence: Q29: "Call hooks only at its top level"; Q30: "Call hooks only at the top level, because React matches them by call order"
findings.fix: Swap Q29 and Q30 so the Rules of Hooks come first, or have Q29 say it follows the Rules of Hooks, explained next.

findings.summary: Q32 relies on Suspense with a fallback before Suspense is explained in Q35 on page 9.
findings.evidence: "Wrap lazy parts in Suspense with a fallback" and `<Suspense fallback={<Spin />}>`
findings.fix: Add a short gloss that Suspense shows a fallback while lazy code loads (see page 9), or move code splitting after Suspense.

findings.summary: Hydration is used in the diagram and in Q38 and the table, but it is never defined.
findings.evidence: Diagram: "'use client'" with sub "hydrates"; Q38: "SSR: per request, then hydrated"; table column "Client JS?" with "Hydrates"
findings.fix: Add a bullet to Q37 or Q38 defining hydration: "the client attaches event handlers and state to server-sent HTML".

findings.summary: The cover title doesn't match the series title, so the carousel is branded two ways.
findings.evidence: series: "40 MOST ASKED REACT INTERVIEW QUESTIONS" vs titles[0]: "React Interview Q&A Bank"; the caption opens with "40 React interview questions"
findings.fix: Retitle page 1 to "40 Most Asked React Interview Questions", or change the series name to "React Interview Q&A Bank" and use that in the caption.

findings.summary: Q3 and Q4 mention layout effects, useEffect and keys before those topics are taught.
findings.evidence: Q3 example "commit: write DOM, run layout fx / after paint: run useEffect"; Q4 "Use `<Fragment key=...>` when rendering lists"
findings.fix: Mark these as forward references ("effects: page 4", "keys: page 5") or trim them from page 2.

findings.summary: Q12 mentions memo and effect deps, which are not introduced until later pages.
findings.evidence: "Mutation also breaks memo and effect deps"
findings.fix: Say "also breaks memoization and effect dependencies, covered later", or drop the bullet until those pages.

findings.summary: Q14 asserts that missing deps cause a stale closure but gives no example, and the term is not defined.
findings.evidence: "Missing deps leave a **stale closure** with old values"; the example shows only `[]`, no array, and `[a, b]`
findings.fix: Add an example of an effect that reads `count` with `[]` deps and keeps logging the initial value.

findings.summary: Q16 uses a ref (`ref.current`) before refs are taught on page 6.
findings.fix: Add a comment that `ref` points at a DOM node (see page 6), or show the ref declaration.

findings.summary: Q33 names SSR as an error-boundary gap, but SSR is not explained until Q38 on page 10.
findings.fix: Gloss SSR as server-side rendering here, or point forward to Q38.
